banks.explain_sca: You'll be redirected to your bank to authenticate (SCA).
banks.explain_readonly: Only account movements are read — money can never be moved.
banks.explain_expiry: The permission expires in 90–180 days and will need re-linking.
banks.explain_selfhosted: Your data stays in this self-hosted instance.
banks.label: Label
banks.delete_confirm: Remove this connection and its pending movements?
banks.rules_description: Automatically suggest a category and direction for incoming movements. Confirming a movement also remembers its counterparty.
banks.truncated_note: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} — refine filters to see the rest

recurring.title: Recurring
recurring.description: Templates that automatically create transactions on a weekly, monthly, or yearly schedule.

budget.title: Budgets
budget.description: Set spending limits per category. Monthly applies to the selected month; annual spans the whole year.
budget.monthly_description: Spending limits for the selected month. The projection extrapolates current pace to month-end.

networth.title: Wealth
networth.snapshots_description: Point-in-time totals of every asset class and active liability. Take one whenever you want to track progress.
networth.movements_description: Contributions, withdrawals, and debt payments between snapshots. Used to attribute Wealth changes to flows versus market returns.
networth.flows_description: How your money moves: capital reallocations and cash adjustments.
networth.cash_no_adjustments: Add an adjustment to start tracking cash. Until then, cash carries over from the previous snapshot.
networth.cash_end_of_day_hint: This is your cash at the end of the selected day; only flows dated after it adjust the estimate.
networth.cash_breakdown: Since your last adjustment on {{date}} ({{amount}}), net flows {{net}} → estimated {{estimate}}.
networth.liabilities_description: Recurring debts (mortgage, loans, credit lines). Their balance is reflected in your Wealth snapshots, subtracted from your net worth. They are not linked to transactions — they neither create nor consume expenses. Inactive items are hidden from new snapshots.
networth.evolution_description: Wealth, assets, and liabilities plotted over time from your snapshots.
networth.allocation_description: Share of each asset class in your most recent snapshot.
networth.delta_warning: One or more values changed by more than 50%. Confirm to save.
networth.assets_description: Named things you own with a value (property, vehicles, valuables). Their value is reflected in your Wealth snapshots, added to your net worth. Each keeps its own dated value history. Inactive items are hidden from new snapshots.
networth.inactive_hint: Uncheck to mark sold/inactive — hidden from new snapshots.
networth.amortizable_balance_hint: Balance is computed from the loan schedule — open 📅 to manage it.
networth.loan_intro: A debt can contain one or more loans (e.g. a fixed-rate loan and a variable-rate loan). Its total balance and monthly instalment are the sum of the loans. Save a loan to compute its schedule.
networth.charge_day_hint: Day of the month the instalment is charged (1–31; a value past the month length uses the last day).
networth.no_parts: No loans yet. Add one to build the debt.
networth.charge_day_required: Charge day is required for a debt that contains loans.
networth.charged_empty: None yet — actual payments appear after the next charge day.
networth.start_mode_current_help: Enter the outstanding balance and its date; the schedule projects forward. Simple, exact balance, no past history.
networth.start_mode_origin_help: Enter the original principal and the loan's start date; the full schedule is generated from origin, including past payments. The current balance is computed.
networth.original_principal_help: The amount originally borrowed at the loan's start.
networth.origin_date_help: The loan's start date; the schedule is generated from here through the end.
networth.payment_history_hint: Payment rows are read-only. Correct via prepayment, rate revision or re-anchor.
networth.re_anchor_help: Set the real outstanding balance at a date; the schedule reprojects from there and keeps the past history.
networth.method_hint_interest_only: Interest only; the whole principal is due at the end.
networth.method_hint_zero: No interest; equal principal each month.
networth.outstanding_principal_help: The current outstanding balance of this loan — not the original amount borrowed.
networth.start_date_help: The date the outstanding balance is measured; the schedule projects forward from here (usually today).
networth.term_end_help: Enter either a term or an end date — each converts to the other.
networth.instalment_help: Or enter the instalment instead of a term; the term is computed.
networth.rate_revisions_help: Add a revision (date + new rate), including past dates; the schedule recalculates from each.
networth.prepayments_help: A one-off extra payment that reduces the debt. Reduce term keeps the instalment and finishes earlier; reduce instalment keeps the term and lowers the instalment.
networth.revaluation_explainer: Net worth minus cumulative contributions — the share attributable to market changes.
networth.no_movements_hint: Record Wealth movements to see how much of your growth came from contributions versus market changes.
networth.value_source_computed_hint: Auto-filled from your portfolio holdings valued at the snapshot date. Edit the value to override it.
networth.stale_prices_disclaimer: Some portfolio prices are stale or missing at this date; computed values use the last known price. You can override any value.
networth.auto_snapshot_description: Create Wealth snapshots on a schedule so tracking does not depend on remembering. Market classes are pre-filled from your portfolio; other classes are carried over from the previous snapshot for you to update.
networth.value_source_carried_over_hint: Carried over from the previous snapshot by an automatic snapshot. Edit it whenever it changes.

portfolio.title: Portfolio

portfolio.evolution_description: Market value of the portfolio over time, next to the remaining invested amount (drops when you sell).
portfolio.new_holding_hint: Type a symbol and pick a match to enable automatic prices. You can also create the holding unlinked and link it later.
portfolio.empty: No holdings yet. Create one to start tracking your investments.
portfolio.avg_cost_tooltip: Average purchase cost per unit = cost basis ÷ quantity

portfolio.fund_no_provider: Funds have no automatic price provider yet.
portfolio.link_optional_hint: Optional: pick a match to fetch prices automatically. Skipping keeps the holding unlinked.
portfolio.roi_twr_description: Time-weighted return: chains the daily market returns between trades, so contributions and withdrawals are not counted as performance.

lendings.header_description: Money you lend to others — tracking only. Not counted toward your Wealth (a deliberate choice) and not linked to transactions.
lendings.confirm_settle: Mark this lending as settled? Interest will stop accruing.
lendings.confirm_write_off: Declare this lending written off? Interest stops accruing and it is excluded from outstanding totals.
lendings.home_note: Payments apply to interest first, then principal. These amounts are tracked separately from your Wealth.

analytics.trailing_description: Income, expenses, and savings rate for the last 12 months ending this month.

notifications.help_show: How do I get a bot token and chat ID?
notifications.help_step1_body: Open a chat with @BotFather, send /newbot, follow the prompts, and copy the token it gives you (looks like 123456789:AA…).
notifications.help_step2_title: 2. Add the bot to your chat
notifications.help_step2_body: For a private message, open your bot and press Start. For a group, add the bot as a member. For a channel, add it as an administrator so it can post.
notifications.help_step3_body: getUpdates only lists chats the bot has already heard from, so first send it a message: in a private chat press Start (or send /start); in a group, add the bot and then send any message. Now open the URL below (with your token) in a browser and read result[].message.chat.id. Group/channel IDs are negative.
notifications.help_step3_hint: Tip: bots like @userinfobot or @RawDataBot will also tell you a chat ID.

export.title: Export everything
export.description: Download a single ZIP containing transactions, recurring templates, movements, snapshots, lendings, and their payments — one CSV per dataset. The same files re-import cleanly.

import.title: Data import & export
import.settings_description: Import previously exported CSVs back into this household, or download a full backup as a ZIP.
import.page_description: Upload a CSV exported from this app. Validation runs first; nothing is written until you confirm.
import.transactions_description: Same format as Transactions → Export CSV. Duplicates of existing data are skipped automatically; rows duplicated within the same file are all imported with a numeric suffix appended to the description.
import.snapshots_description: Same format as Snapshots → Export CSV. Each date is one snapshot; choose what to do if a date already exists.
import.portfolio_description: One row per purchase lot; rows sharing asset_class and symbol become one holding. Duplicate lots are skipped.
import.movements_description: Same format as Movements → Export CSV. Duplicates of existing data are skipped automatically; rows duplicated within the same file are all imported with a numeric suffix appended to the description.
import.recurring_description: Same format as Recurring → Export CSV. Imports never advance the materialization clock — new templates fire from their start_date the next time you run them.
import.lendings_description: Same format as Lent → Export lendings CSV. Duplicates (same borrower, start date and principal) are skipped automatically.
import.lending_payments_description: Same format as Lent → Export payments CSV. Each row locates its lending by borrower and lending start date.
import.assets_description: Same format as Assets → Export CSV. Each asset is matched by name; value entries already present are skipped, so re-importing an export is safe.
import.liabilities_named_description: Same format as Liabilities → Export CSV. Each liability is matched by name; balance entries already present are skipped.
import.amortization_description: Rebuilds the schedules of amortizable liabilities: parts, rate revisions, prepayments and the generated instalments. Import liabilities first. Existing rows are skipped, so re-importing an export is safe.
import.duplicate_policy: If a date already has a snapshot
import.errors_truncated: Only the first 500 errors are shown.
import.skipped_found: {{count}} rows match existing data and will be skipped
import.adjusted_found: {{count}} rows are duplicated within the file — their descriptions will be tagged with (2), (3), … so each one stays unique

format.ai_hint: Tip: paste this whole reference into any AI assistant (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, …) together with your bank statement, PDF account summary or other report, and ask it to produce a CSV that follows exactly this format. Then come back here, validate the result, and import it.

tx.intro: European-CSV dialect: UTF-8, semicolon (;) column separator, comma (,) as decimal mark, RFC-4180 quoting (wrap a field in double quotes if it contains ;, " or a line break; escape " by doubling). First row is the literal header shown below; one transaction per data row. Amounts are always positive — the sign of the operation comes from the direction column.
tx.date: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-05-25). The day the transaction occurred.
tx.direction: Either income or expense (lowercase). Must match the kind of the chosen category_code.
tx.category_code: One of the codes listed below. income.* codes are valid only with direction=income; the rest are expense.
tx.amount: Positive decimal. Comma is the canonical decimal separator (e.g. 12,34); dot is also accepted on import. No thousand separators, no currency symbol. Up to 2 decimals are stored.
tx.description: Optional free text up to 500 characters. Leave the field empty if there is no description.
tx.created_at: Optional ISO instant in UTC (e.g. 2026-05-25T10:30:00Z). Defaults to now if empty.
tx.updated_at: Optional ISO instant in UTC. Defaults to now if empty.
tx.unknown_category_note: If a category_code in your CSV is not listed above, the row will be rejected. Create it first as a Custom category in Settings → Categories.
tx.dedup: Duplicate detection: rows whose (date, direction, category_code, amount, description) match an existing transaction are skipped automatically.
tx.in_file_dedup: If the same row appears more than once within the file, every copy is imported. To keep each transaction distinct, “ (2)”, “ (3)”, … is appended to the description of the duplicates (or “(2)”, “(3)”, … if the description was empty). The preview lists every row whose description was changed before you confirm. Trade-off: once an identical row exists in the database, every later upload of that same row is skipped — even when it appears twice in the new file alongside the existing one. To add a genuine second copy, give it a distinct description or delete the existing row first.

snap.intro: European-CSV dialect: UTF-8, semicolon (;) column separator, comma (,) as decimal mark, RFC-4180 quoting. First row is the literal header shown below. A Wealth snapshot on a given date is built by grouping rows that share the same date. Each snapshot must include a value row for every asset class AND for every active liability of the household, otherwise the whole date is rejected.
snap.date: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD. All rows with the same date form one snapshot.
snap.note: Optional free text. Must be identical on every row for the same date (otherwise the date is rejected).
snap.kind: Either asset or liability (lowercase). Determines what key is expected on this row.
snap.key: If kind=asset: one of the asset class codes below. If kind=liability: the exact name of an active liability defined in this household (case-sensitive).
snap.value: Non-negative decimal (0 is allowed). Comma is the canonical decimal separator; dot is also accepted on import.
snap.asset_codes_note: Asset class codes are predefined and cannot be customized. Rows referencing a code that is not listed above will be rejected.
snap.liabilities_note: Liability rows must reference the exact name of a liability that already exists and is active in this household. Inactive or unknown names will be rejected. Create or activate liabilities in Wealth → Liabilities first.
snap.no_liabilities: No active liabilities in this household yet.
snap.rules: Per-date rules: every asset class must have exactly one value row, every active liability must have exactly one value row, and no asset/liability key may repeat within the same date.

rec.intro: European-CSV dialect: UTF-8, semicolon (;) column separator, comma (,) as decimal mark, RFC-4180 quoting. First row is the literal header shown below; one recurring template per data row. Imports do not advance the materialization clock — newly imported templates fire from their start_date the next time you run them.
rec.direction: Either income or expense (lowercase). Must match the kind of the chosen category_code.
rec.category_code: One of the codes listed below.
rec.amount: Positive decimal. Comma is the canonical decimal separator (e.g. 45,00); dot is also accepted on import. Up to 2 decimals are stored.
rec.description: Optional free text up to 500 characters.
rec.cadence: One of weekly, monthly, or yearly (lowercase). Determines which of the day/month columns is required.
rec.day_of_week: 1-7 (1=Monday … 7=Sunday). Required when cadence=weekly. Must be empty otherwise.
rec.day_of_month: 1-31. Required when cadence=monthly. Must be empty otherwise.
rec.month_of_year: 1-12. Required when cadence=yearly. Must be empty otherwise.
rec.day_of_month_yearly: 1-31. Required when cadence=yearly. Must be empty otherwise.
rec.start_date: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD. The earliest date this template can fire.
rec.end_date: Optional ISO date YYYY-MM-DD. The template stops firing after this date. Must be ≥ start_date.
rec.active: true or false. Inactive templates are kept but never fire automatically.
rec.dedup: Duplicate detection: a row is skipped automatically if every column matches an existing template (direction, category, amount, cadence, all day/month fields, start/end dates, active, and description).
rec.in_file_dedup: If two rows inside the file are identical in every column, the duplicates get “ (2)”, “ (3)”, … appended to their description so each one stays distinct.

mov.intro: European-CSV dialect: UTF-8, semicolon (;) column separator, comma (,) as decimal mark, RFC-4180 quoting. First row is the literal header shown below; one movement per data row. Movements record contributions or withdrawals against an asset class, or payments against a liability — they do not affect transaction totals.
mov.type: One of contribution, withdrawal, or debt_payment (lowercase).
mov.asset_class_code: Required when type is contribution or withdrawal — one of the asset class codes below. Must be empty when type=debt_payment.
mov.liability_name: Required when type=debt_payment — exact name of an existing active liability in this household. Must be empty when type is contribution or withdrawal.
mov.amount: Positive decimal. Comma is the canonical decimal separator; dot is also accepted on import. No sign — the type column determines the effect.
mov.description: Optional free text up to 500 characters.
mov.created_at: Optional ISO instant in UTC (e.g. 2026-05-25T10:30:00Z). Defaults to now if empty.
mov.dedup: Duplicate detection: rows whose (date, type, target, amount, description) match an existing movement are skipped automatically. target is the asset_class_code or the liability.
mov.in_file_dedup: If the same row appears more than once within the file, every copy is imported. To keep each movement distinct, “ (2)”, “ (3)”, … is appended to the description of the duplicates (or “(2)”, “(3)”, … if the description was empty). The preview lists every row whose description was changed before you confirm. Trade-off: once an identical row exists in the database, every later upload of that same row is skipped — even when it appears twice in the new file alongside the existing one. To add a genuine second copy, give it a distinct description or delete the existing row first.

lending.intro: European-CSV dialect: UTF-8, semicolon (;) column separator, comma (,) decimal, RFC-4180 quoting, ISO dates. The first row is the literal header; one lending per row. Amounts are always positive.
lending.borrower_name: Free text. Name of the person you lent to.
lending.principal_amount: Positive decimal. Amount lent, in the household currency.
lending.start_date: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Date the money was lent.
lending.annual_interest_rate: Decimal in percentage points (e.g. 5,00 = 5%). Required when interest_type is simple or compound; empty otherwise.
lending.compounding_period: monthly or yearly. Required when interest_type=compound; empty otherwise.
lending.description: Optional free text up to 500 characters.
lending.status: active, settled or written_off. Optional; defaults to active.
lending.dedup: Duplicate detection: rows whose (borrower_name, start_date, principal_amount) match an existing lending are skipped automatically.

lending_payment.intro: European-CSV dialect: UTF-8, semicolon (;) column separator, comma (,) decimal, ISO dates. The first row is the literal header; one payment per row. Amounts are always positive.
lending_payment.borrower_name: Must match an existing lending's borrower_name.
lending_payment.lending_start_date: Must match that lending's start_date; together with the borrower it locates the lending.
lending_payment.payment_date: ISO YYYY-MM-DD of the payment received.
lending_payment.matching_note: If multiple lendings match the (borrower_name, loan_start_date) tuple, the row is rejected as ambiguous.
lending_payment.dedup: Duplicate detection: rows whose (borrower_name, loan_start_date, payment_date, amount, description) match an existing payment are skipped automatically.

portfolio.intro: One row per trade (BUY or SELL). Rows that share asset_class and symbol belong to the same holding, which is created automatically. Net quantity, remaining cost basis and realized P&L are computed by replaying the trades (FIFO). For pricing, the easiest path is to import first and then link each holding from the app using its search — leave provider and provider_symbol blank. Those columns exist mainly so an export keeps its links on re-import.
portfolio.asset_class: One of crypto, etf, stock, fund.
portfolio.symbol: Your identifier for the holding (e.g. BTC, WEBN, AAPL). Uppercased automatically.
portfolio.label: Display name for the holding; taken from the first row.
portfolio.native_currency: ISO 4217 currency the instrument trades in. Defaults to EUR.
portfolio.isin: Optional 12-character ISIN; used to auto-link stocks/ETFs. Leave blank for crypto.
portfolio.provider: Optional price source: coingecko, yahoo, eodhd or twelvedata. Best left blank: after importing, open the holding and use the in-app search to link it — that finds the exact provider symbol for you. Only fill these in if you already know the precise identifiers.
portfolio.provider_symbol: The holding's exact identifier at that provider (e.g. bitcoin for CoinGecko, WEBN.DE for Yahoo). Required whenever provider is set. Hard to guess by hand — prefer linking after import via search.
portfolio.quantity: Units bought; positive, comma decimal, up to 12 decimals.
portfolio.unit_price: Price per unit in cost_currency (purchase price for BUY, sale price for SELL); comma decimal.
portfolio.cost_currency: Currency of unit_price and fee. Defaults to native_currency.
portfolio.fee: Optional trade fee in cost_currency (added to cost on BUY, subtracted from proceeds on SELL).
portfolio.type: BUY or SELL. Empty defaults to BUY.
portfolio.grouping: Multiple trades of one holding = multiple rows with the same asset_class and symbol. Sells must be covered by earlier buys.
portfolio.dedup: Rows matching an existing trade on type, asset class, symbol, date, quantity, unit price and currency are skipped, so re-importing an export is safe.
portfolio.note: Optional free-text note for the trade, up to 500 characters. Not part of the duplicate check.

assets.intro: One asset per name, with zero or more dated value rows. Repeat the name on each value row; leave value_date and value empty to import an asset with no history yet.
assets.name: Asset name; identifies the asset (reused if it already exists).
assets.active: true or false. Inactive assets are excluded from new snapshots.
assets.value_date: ISO YYYY-MM-DD of a value observation. Optional.
assets.value: Value on that date; comma decimal. Required when value_date is set.
assets.dedup: A value row already present (same date and value) is skipped, so re-importing an export is safe.

liab.intro: One liability per name, with zero or more dated balance rows. Amortizable liabilities carry their schedule separately (Amortization import); leave their balance rows empty here.
liab.name: Liability name; identifies the liability (reused if it already exists).
liab.active: true or false. Inactive liabilities are excluded from new snapshots.
liab.amortizable: true when the balance is computed by an amortization schedule.
liab.charge_day: For amortizable liabilities, day of month (1–31) the instalment is charged.
liab.balance_date: ISO YYYY-MM-DD of a manual balance. Optional (empty for amortizable).
liab.balance: Balance on that date; comma decimal. Required when balance_date is set.
liab.dedup: A balance row already present (same date and value) is skipped, so re-importing an export is safe.

amort.intro: Rebuilds the schedules of amortizable liabilities. Each row is one record: a part, a rate revision, a prepayment, or a generated instalment (entry). The liability must already exist and part rows must precede their revisions/prepayments/entries.
amort.liability_name: Name of an existing amortizable liability.
amort.part_label: Identifies the part within the liability; keep it stable across a part's rows.
amort.record_type: One of part, revision, prepayment, entry.
amort.date: ISO YYYY-MM-DD: start date (part), effective date (revision), date (prepayment), charge date (entry).
amort.fields: Remaining columns are used per record type: part → method, principal, annual_rate, term_months, instalment, start_mode, anchor_date, anchor_balance; revision → annual_rate; prepayment → amount, mode; entry → principal, interest, resulting_balance.
amort.dedup: Existing parts (by start date, principal and method), revisions, prepayments and entries are skipped, so re-importing an export is safe.
